title: Fusion Doc
summary: Builds Swami's Fusion Doc dashboard: a vibe-dashboard page documenting every parameter of one Autodesk Fusion command or toolpath, from a tab, group and parameter JSON plus its Autodesk help-page URL, with an Input section that can load another command in the browser.
what_it_is: A Claude skill that builds a **reference dashboard** for one Fusion command or CAM toolpath dialog, such as 2D Offset Roughing, Adaptive Clearing or Extrude. It starts from a **parameter JSON** (tabs, then groups, then parameter names, in dialog order) and the URL of the command's Autodesk product-documentation page. Swami makes that JSON with a command in the **Autodesk Assistant** AI inside Fusion.

Claude researches the help page and writes a `notes.json` with a plain-language description and a tip for every parameter, plus a glossary. The skill's build script embeds both JSON files in the page, and the page **renders itself in the browser**. That is what lets its **Input** section load a different JSON or URL and rebuild every data-driven section, with descriptions carried over wherever names match. Like every vibe-dashboard, it also has Search, a Mind Map, a Glossary and an audio overview.
why: A Fusion dialog can hold a hundred settings spread over several tabs. One page that lists every parameter where it lives, explains it, and links to Autodesk's own reference makes a command much faster to learn and to look things up in.

what_it_does.text: Run with no inputs, it builds nothing and asks for the parameter JSON and the help-page URL.
Converts a JSON of another shape to `operation` plus `tabs`, and says how. Given only a URL, it tries to read the page and builds the JSON from its headings, showing it before building.
Writes what each parameter does and a tip, a description for each group, and an intro, cross-reference, focus and use-when line for each tab, usually plus a step-by-step setup workflow section.
A Parameter Map at a Glance section with a tabs table and a table of every group and its parameters.
A collapsible tree of command, tab, group and parameter, with sticky level buttons, jump links to each table row, and hover tooltips.
One section per dialog tab, with a table per group. A uniform tab, where every group has the same few fields (like Heights), gets one table instead.
Lets a viewer load another parameter JSON (file or paste) and URL; the page saves it in that browser and rebuilds. "reset to original" goes back to the built-in JSON.
Links to the Autodesk help page and any other sources, and shows the parameter JSON verbatim.
Adds vibe-dashboard's Search section, Mind Map, table fitting and a Glossary, plus a spoken audio overview that hides itself when another command is loaded through Input.
Tests the page in a headless browser at two widths: no page errors or colour clashes, every tree link lands on a table row, tables fit, summary rows link, and every glossary term is used.

triggers: Uploading a tab, group and parameter JSON with a help.autodesk.com link

how_to_use.step: Run your command in the **Autodesk Assistant** inside Fusion to get the dialog's tabs, groups and parameter names as JSON, for example `{"operation": "Adaptive Clearing", "tabs": {"Tool": {"Feed & Speed": ["Spindle Speed"]}}}`.
Copy the command's Autodesk help-page link from your browser.
Run `/fusion-doc` and attach or paste the JSON and the link. With nothing attached, Claude asks for both and waits.
Claude reads the help page and writes the notes: every parameter, group and tab, a setup workflow, and a glossary.
Claude builds the page, records the audio overview, checks it in a headless browser, and publishes it as an artifact.
To view another command with the same page, load its JSON and URL in the Input section. The page remembers it in your browser until you reset.
Ask for changes. Claude edits the notes or JSON and rebuilds; the HTML is never hand-edited.

how_to_use_windows.step: Building happens in Claude's workspace and the page opens in any browser, so the steps are the same on Windows.
Run the same Autodesk Assistant command in Fusion on Windows, and attach the JSON from File Explorer; downloads land in `C:\Users\<name>\Downloads` by default.

capabilities.text: Documents any Fusion command or toolpath dialog, from design features to CAM operations.
Gives every parameter a description and a tip, in dialog order.
The Input section turns one published page into a viewer for other commands' JSON, with no rebuild.
The hierarchy tree jumps straight to any tab, group or parameter row.
Search, the Mind Map and the Glossary make every parameter quick to find.

limitations.text: help.autodesk.com pages are script-heavy and can come back thin; then the notes rely on general Fusion knowledge and say so.
A command loaded through Input only gets descriptions where names match the original; extras and the custom intro are hidden.
What Input loads is remembered only in that browser.
The Autodesk Assistant command that makes the parameter JSON isn't written down in the skill yet.
The audio describes the original command, so it hides when another command is loaded through Input.

gotchas.text: The sections are drawn in the browser, so the narration outline comes from a rendered copy of the page, made with a short Playwright command in the skill.
Glossary terms must appear in descriptions, tips or intros; parameter and group names never link, so they don't count.
Run with nothing attached, it must ask and wait, never build an example page.
Every group must be a non-empty list of parameter names; anything else is rejected, in the build and in the Input section.
A tab whose groups all share the same four or fewer fields becomes one table, so notes for it take a typical value, not a description and tip.
Always rebuild from a fresh template copy; the script refuses a copy it already built.
Sections are rendered from the embedded JSON at load time, so hand edits to the HTML are lost. Recover the JSON from the published page if the scratchpad is gone.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the Fusion doc skill. It builds a reference dashboard for every parameter of one Fusion command, from a list of its tabs, groups and parameters, made with Autodesk Assistant, plus its Autodesk help page
spoken.What It Is: What the skill is: Claude writes a description and a tip for every parameter, and the page draws itself in your browser, so its input section can load another command. It also has search, a mind map, a glossary and audio
spoken.What It Does: Ten jobs, from asking for inputs and writing notes to the parameter map, the hierarchy tree, tab sections, the input section, references, search and audio, and checks
spoken.How to Use It: Seven steps, from getting the JSON from Autodesk Assistant and the help page link to [research](/ɹˈiːsɜːtʃ/), building, using the input section, and edits. On Windows the steps are the same
spoken.Skills It Depends On: Vibe dashboard is required for the template. Fusion doc to JSON and Fusion cam settings are related
spoken.Programs It Depends On: Fusion with Autodesk Assistant and a browser on your computer, plus Python, a headless browser and the [Kokoro](/kˈoʊkoʊɹoʊ/) voice in Claude's workspace
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It covers any command and every parameter, one page can view other commands, and it's easy to search. But help pages can come back thin, the Assistant command isn't written down yet, and the audio only fits the original command
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None. Its pages are simply backed up each night with all the others
spoken.Where It Runs: Swami has run it in the desktop app linked to his Mac. The other surfaces should work too, but are still untested
spoken.Gotchas: Seven traps, from writing the narration from a rendered copy and where glossary terms must appear to the input JSON's shape and uniform tabs
spoken.Other Requirements: The parameter JSON and ideally the help page link, code execution, web fetch and artifacts in Claude, and any Mac or Windows computer
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint. There are no open questions
